summary: The adaptive strictly convex cost theorem is proved without mathematical errors or gaps. The target-merging argument gives the lattice-complete vertex hull and intrinsic parity bound; the finite strict dual correctly characterizes the entire minimizing face, including structural zeros; entropy stationarity and the proved active-set inclusion give the share-potential and row-logarithm inequalities for arbitrary positive barycentric representations. The roof extension preserves every lattice zero, and the normalization and cost comparisons use the original table consistently. Singleton supports, rank-zero and lower-rank hulls, boundary cells, forced entries, and affine-dependent components are covered. The finite-data equivalence uses exactly part 1 of the supplied accepted predecessor c300e9d112cefeb0.
